strengths: Novel theoretical identification that Tweedie-based training-free guidance is suboptimal (Proposition 3.2), with clear decomposition into low-density, reward, and KL regularization terms

Creative and well-motivated integration of stochastic optimal control and Stein variational inference for diffusion guidance; back-and-forth correction trick elegantly avoids expensive Jacobian computations
Strong empirical results with dramatic improvements (e.g., 2.933% → 25.744% for 5ht1b), convincing ablation study showing SDG without Stein correction often performs worse than baselines

Comprehensive experimental analysis including sampling dynamics visualization (Figures 5, 9-10), multiple evaluation metrics, extreme low-density experiments (40% validity at α_E=0.7), and molecular docking pose visualization
Clear presentation with effective illustration (Figure 1), explicit algorithm description (Algorithm 1), and thorough experimental details in appendix including hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Loose theoretical guarantees: Proposition 3.2 provides upper bound with D_KL(q||p) but offers no analysis of bound tightness; only one SVGD step per timestep applied without convergence analysis; approximation error from back-and-forth correction not quantified; no formal proof connecting KL divergence minimization to improved guidance performance

Severely limited experimental scope with validation on only one domain (molecular generation); while Section 3.4 extends to graphs, this is not experimentally validated beyond molecular graphs; claims of broad applicability unsupported
No quantification of computational overhead; Algorithm 1 requires O(N²) kernel and gradient computations but wall-clock time comparisons with baselines absent; scalability analysis missing

High hyperparameter sensitivity with substantial variation across targets (Table 2: α_X from 0.10 to 0.42; α_A from 0.20 to 0.42); unclear whether equal tuning effort invested in baseline methods; no systematic sensitivity analysis provided

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: Figure 5b shows classifier overestimation without Stein correction but root cause not deeply analyzed; formal connection between KL divergence minimization and reward estimation reliability not established; limited comparison to recent training-free baselines (DPS cited but not compared)

Theory-practice gap: theoretical analysis assumes closed-form posteriors and well-specified classifiers but robustness to classifier approximation errors not discussed; convergence properties of single-step SVGD per timestep across full diffusion trajectory not analyzed

strengths: Novel theoretical framework combining Stochastic Optimal Control with Stein variational inference for training-free diffusion guidance, with formal propositions establishing value function bounds and optimal control decomposition
Creative back-and-forth Stein correction mechanism that elegantly approximates the computationally expensive SOC formulation while maintaining theoretical connection (Corollary 3.5)

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (images and molecules) with systematic ablation studies (Figures 7-14) and temporal dynamics analysis demonstrating consistent improvements

Strong empirical results on important application: molecular sampling achieves novel hit ratio of 0.156 vs. near-zero for baselines (Table 2), with proven robustness under extreme low-density conditions
Honest treatment of limitations including computational overhead analysis (Table 6), reward overestimation issues, and ablation under varying low-density levels
weaknesses: Theoretical contributions lack actionable guarantees about when/why SDG outperforms alternatives; Proposition 3.2's upper bound includes loosely-bounding KL divergence term without convergence analysis
Significant computational overhead (~85% runtime increase in Table 6) not adequately justified relative to sometimes modest empirical gains (e.g., 54.0% vs 50.1% accuracy with substantial added cost)
Incremental novelty: primarily combines well-established techniques (Stein VI, SOC, score-based diffusion) through a novel cost functional rather than introducing fundamental new concepts
Limited experimental scope: images evaluated primarily on CIFAR-10, molecular sampling on only 3 protein targets; missing comparisons with recent methods like FREED and SVGD-based guidance approaches

Presentation issues: Algorithm 1 (core algorithmic contribution) relegated to appendix; relationship between theoretical Propositions and practical algorithm unclear; key assumptions (Lemma 3.3's Gaussian forward kernel) not explicitly stated in main text

Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned despite method complexity; hyperparameter choices (Table 4) lack justification; cascade of approximations (Tweedie→SOC→Stein correction) has unanalyzed cumulative error

Particle update saturation (acknowledged in Section C.3.6) suggests unresolved fundamental limitations in high dimensions; guidance quality critically depends on score model accuracy without thorough dependency analysis
